chunks: And from his words (peace be upon him), in which he exhorts his companions to jihad.
He exhorts his companions to jihad.

key_terms.أَصْحَابَهُ: His companions, referring to the close followers of Imam Ali.
key_terms.جِهَاد: Striving or exertion in the path of God, often referring to military or spiritual struggle.

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali say to his companions regarding jihad?
ai.summary: In this passage from Nahj al-Balagha, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) addresses his companions, framing jihad not merely as military engagement but as a comprehensive spiritual and physical struggle (mujahada) essential for upholding divine truth. This exhortation reflects the Shia understanding of jihad as a continuous effort, balancing the inner purification of the soul with the outer defense of the community, a concept deeply rooted in the early Islamic context of the Caliphate's consolidation. The narration underscores the virtue of steadfastness (sabr) and the moral responsibility of believers to strive in God's path, aligning with the broader Shia emphasis on action coupled with knowledge.
